# Surface and Mesh Extraction

Also called: Gaussian Mesh Extraction, 3DGS Meshing, Gaussian Segmentation

## Overview
This family provides methods to extract explicit geometric representations (meshes) or semantic segments from trained [3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS)](#1174-3d-gaussian-splatting-3dgs.md) models without retraining the underlying radiance field [3692-gaussian-opacity-fields-gof-mesh-extraction.md], [7411-distance-based-gaussian-splatting.md], [11513-2d-lift-3d-scene-segmentation.md]. It solves the problem of converting implicit, volumetric Gaussian primitives into standard triangle meshes or editable semantic groups, enabling downstream applications like collision detection, physics simulation, and targeted scene editing. The methods differ in their geometric priors: GOF uses volumetric density accumulation, MeshGS uses explicit mesh proximity, and 2D-Lift uses multi-view semantic voting.

## Shared principles
All methods operate on a trained set of $N$ 3D Gaussian primitives $\mathcal{G} = \{g_1, \dots, g_N\}$, where each primitive $g_i$ is defined by its center $\boldsymbol{\mu}_i$, covariance $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_i$, opacity $o_i$, and [spherical harmonics](#5603-spherical-harmonics.md) coefficients $\mathbf{c}_i$ [Parent]. The core challenge is that Gaussians are volumetric and non-intersecting by design, whereas meshes are surface-based and intersecting. Therefore, all methods require a discretization or classification step to map the continuous Gaussian distribution to discrete elements (voxels, surface normals, or labels).

## Subtopics

### [Gaussian Opacity Fields (GOF) Mesh Extraction](3692-gaussian-opacity-fields-gof-mesh-extraction.md)
A method to extract a 3-D triangulated mesh from a trained Gaussian model by building a volumetric density field and extracting an isosurface. It differs from [Distance-based Gaussian Splatting](7411-distance-based-gaussian-splatting.md) by relying on opacity-based density accumulation rather than signed distance functions, and from [2D-Lift-3D Scene Segmentation](11513-2d-lift-3d-scene-segmentation.md) by operating directly on the 3D primitive structure rather than lifting 2D features. Choose this when a watertight mesh is required for geometric processing and no external mesh prior exists.

### [Distance-based Gaussian Splatting](7411-distance-based-gaussian-splatting.md)
[Distance-based Gaussian Splatting](#7411-distance-based-gaussian-splatting.md) (MeshGS) bridges the gap between large-scale explicit triangle meshes and volumetric Gaussian splats by classifying primitives as tightly-bound or loosely-bound based on their distance to the mesh surface. It solves the problem of rendering high-fidelity appearance while maintaining geometric consistency with a lightweight mesh, specifically addressing artifacts where strict binding fails to capture severe mesh inaccuracies. Unlike sibling methods that may rely on opacity fields or 2D lifting for segmentation, this method explicitly uses mesh proximity to prune occluded splats and align tightly-bound splats with surface normals. Choose this when a coarse mesh prior is available and high-fidelity rendering of complex geometry is needed.

### [2D-Lift-3D Scene Segmentation](11513-2d-lift-3d-scene-segmentation.md)
This method segments 3D Gaussian primitives in a volume visualization scene by lifting 2D segmentation masks from reference views into 3D space. It solves the problem of applying distinct editing effects (color, opacity, lighting) to specific regions of a scene represented by millions of Gaussians. Unlike sibling methods that optimize learnable feature vectors for segmentation, this approach is training-free, relying on multi-view label voting to assign labels to primitives. Choose this when semantic editing or object-level manipulation is required without geometric extraction.

## Background
The extraction of geometry from 3D [Gaussian Splatting](#946-gaussian-splatting.md) is a recent development following the introduction of 3DGS [Parent]. Traditional radiance fields (NeRFs) are difficult to mesh directly due to their implicit nature. Early attempts used density thresholding on voxelized fields. The GOF method [3692-gaussian-opacity-fields-gof-mesh-extraction.md] adapts this by accumulating Gaussian opacity into a voxel grid. MeshGS [7411-distance-based-gaussian-splatting.md] introduces a hybrid approach using existing mesh priors. 2D-Lift [11513-2d-lift-3d-scene-segmentation.md] leverages foundation models like SAM for semantic grouping. These methods enable the use of 3DGS in pipelines requiring explicit geometry, such as robotics and AR/VR asset creation.
